title: Ericsson and ÉTS to advance quantum computing ecosystem in Quebec
excerpt: Partnership aims to address some of the most pressing short-term challenges posed by quantum computing in telecommunications and beyond
content:
Partnership aims to address some of the most pressing short-term challenges posed by quantum computing in telecommunications and beyond

Ericsson Canada and the École de technologie supérieure (ÉTS) are joining forces to advance quantum computing research in Quebec, one of the country’s leading centres of expertise in this field. With support from the Mitacs Accelerate program, the project aims to develop improved quantum computing methods that will enable more efficient use and management of telecommunications networks. It will also help train students and researchers in cutting-edge quantum technologies, supporting Canada’s leadership in this area.

“Quantum computing will open up new possibilities for making telecommunications networks more efficient, and Canada is well positioned to be a major player in this field,” says Nishant Grover, president of Ericsson Canada. “Through our Quantum Research Centre in Montreal and our partnership with ÉTS, supported by Mitacs Accelerate, we are bringing together world-class researchers and industry expertise to advance quantum methods, in a practical way, for the operation of telecommunications networks.”

Image Source: AdobeStock (743681515)

Titled “Towards Evolutionary Variational Quantum Algorithms: A Dissipative Approach to Error Mitigation and Optimization,” the project brings together Professor Jacob Biamonte, an internationally renowned quantum computing researcher, his research team at ÉTS, and researchers from Ericsson’s quantum program, with support from Mitacs. Building on Professor Biamonte’s fundamental contributions to variational quantum computing, the partnership investigates methods to mitigate errors and improve the optimization of quantum algorithms. Using quantum hardware and simulations, the team seeks to increase the reliability and practical performance of quantum computing.

“At ÉTS, we believe that a cutting-edge quantum infrastructure is essential for world-class research, the training of highly qualified personnel, and the growth of the Canadian quantum ecosystem. This partnership with Ericsson empowers our researchers to conduct ambitious work at the forefront of quantum computing, while contributing to Canada’s long-term scientific and technological leadership,” says Kathy Baig, Director General and CEO of ÉTS.
